subject: Implementation trajectory: SDK setup, endpoint migration & rate strategy
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lee <sarah@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-05-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Implementation trajectory: SDK setup, endpoint migration & rate strategy

Hi Sarah / John —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion, here's a focused implementation trajectory to get Acme from sandbox -> production in 6 weeks with minimal app changes. I've attached a short sample-init-snippet.py and a starter mutual-action-plan.xlsx.

High-level milestones (target dates):
- Week 0 (this week): Kickoff + security intake completed (security-evidence-list.pdf attached)
- Week 1: Sandbox SDK integration + basic inference call (tokenization + inference)
- Week 2: Endpoint migration plan & traffic shaping tests (staging)
- Week 3-4: Canary rollout + retry/timeouts tuning + cost profiling
- Week 5-6: Production cutover + runbook handoff + post-cutover SLA review

Immediate asks for the kickoff (before Mon):
1) Confirm which service account you'll use for sandbox access (email or GSuite group)
2) Send the security questionnaire answers or point us to where we can pull docs
3) Share any expected QPS patterns (spiky vs steady) and common request payload size

Quick integration guidance notes (to save time in kickoff):
- SDK: use redwood-python v0.8+; sample-init-snippet.py covers auth, simple generation, and streaming fallback.
- Endpoint migration: keep existing endpoint path stable; we recommend a canary header X-ACME-Canary for traffic split and a short 5% -> 25% -> 100% ramp.
- Retries/timeouts: client timeout = 30s for single-shot generation. Retries: 2 attempts on 5xx with exponential backoff (initial 250ms, factor 2, max 2s) and jitter. Avoid retrying on 4xx or on partial-response errors.
- Rate limiting: throttle with a leaky-bucket on the client side targeting 85% of observed steady throughput; use 429 handling to backoff and push to the queue if requests are non-interactive.

Attachments: sample-init-snippet.py (light examples), mutual-action-plan.xlsx (editable milestones), security-evidence-list.pdf (what we typically need for SOC-type checks).

I'll set a 30-minute kickoff with our implementation lead Vivek for Tue 10:00 PT unless you prefer another slot — please confirm.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

On Fri, May 30, 2025 at 11:40 AM Sarah Lee <sarah@acme-corp.com> wrote:
> Monica — thanks for the clear plan. A few quick clarifications before kickoff:
>
> - Service account: we'll use acme-devs@acme-corp.com for sandbox access, ok?
> - QPS: expected steady ~20 r/s with 5x spikes during batch runs (10–15 minutes), payloads avg ~2.5KB, some up to 25KB.
> - Security: I've uploaded our baseline security intake to our vendor portal (link below) and attached a redacted SOC2 overview. We will need a mapping for data retention and encryption-in-transit details during the call.

Thanks Sarah — that's helpful context. A few implementation-first actions I want to call out so the kickoff is high velocity: 

1) Sandbox access: monica, please send a minimal IAM role suggestion we can apply to acme-devs@acme-corp.com; recommend: role.redwood.sandbox.integration (read/write to sandbox, no billing access).

2) Traffic shaping approach (staging):
   - Canary header: X-ACME-Canary = true for initial 5% traffic
   - Ramp: 5% -> 25% (48h) -> 100% (after 7d of stability)
   - Spike handling: for short-duration 5x spikes, use client-side smoothing with token bucket (burst=4s at steady rate) and queue non-critical batch requests to a separate ingestion endpoint to avoid blocking user-facing traffic.

3) Retries & timeouts (concrete config snippets):
   - client_timeout_ms: 30000
   - retry_policy: attempts=2, base_backoff_ms=250, max_backoff_ms=2000, jitter=true
   - retry_on: 500,502,503,504,429 (only when idempotent or safe-to-replay)

Example snippet (Python):
```
from redwood import RedwoodClient
c = RedwoodClient(api_key="REDACTED", timeout_ms=30000, retry_policy={"attempts":2, "base_backoff_ms":250, "max_backoff_ms":2000, "jitter":True})
resp = c.generate(model="redwood-lite", prompt="hi")
```

4) Endpoint migration notes: keep v1 path intact; create /v2 that validates larger payloads and streaming. We'll support a staged traffic header and provide a migration-checklist to verify tokenization parity (we'll run a token-level diff test).

5) Observability: enable request_id propagation (X-Request-Id) and include per-request token counts in telemetry. We'll provide a dashboard template for latency and cost per 1k tokens.

I've uploaded a starter mutual-action-plan to the shared link (https://drive.redwood.com/s/ACME-RDW-4782-impl) and added column owners for each milestone. Monica — I'll own the SDK integration and can block 1.5 days of eng time the week of the 9th for the canary run. Chloe will lead runbook drafting.

See short checklist I'm pasting below to carry into the kickoff: 
- [ ] Service account + IAM role assigned
- [ ] Sandbox creds validated and sample-init-snippet.py run by Acme devs
- [ ] Tokenization parity test active (dev data)
- [ ] Traffic ramp plan agreed (headers + % schedule)
- [ ] Retry/timeouts set on client-side + doc updated
- [ ] Observability hooks added

Thanks — looking forward to Tue.

--
Vivek Kulkarni
